mainTopic: לינה on סוכות, seven days of תשלומין for עצרת, and why the ברייתא of בל תאחר lists פסח
overview: This amud opens at the end of a דרשה that compares the three רגלים, based on the verse that lists them together. Just as פסח requires לינה (staying overnight in ירושלים), so does סוכות. The source for פסח is the פסוק "ופנית בבקר." The גמרא then asks about the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון, who use that verse for בל תאחר instead. Where do they learn that שבועות has seven days of תשלומין? They learn it from רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא: each holiday is sanctified for the unit by which it is counted, and עצרת is counted in weeks. When challenged that we count days, רבא answers that we count weeks too, and the תורה calls it חג שבועות. The גמרא then asks how the ברייתא of בל תאחר can list פסח, since it has a fixed day. רב חסדא says פסח was mentioned for no reason, and רב ששת says it means שלמי פסח. When challenged that this repeats שלמים, the גמרא begins explaining why both kinds of שלמים were needed, and that explanation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: סוכות requires staying overnight, just like פסח
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the היקש: סוכות is compared to פסח, so it also requires לינה in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the festival of מצות requires staying overnight, so too the festival of סוכות requires staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that compares סוכות to פסח. It says that סוכות, like פסח, requires the pilgrim to stay overnight in ירושלים before going home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of the דרשה that links the three רגלים in one verse. The first half compared שבועות to פסח for תשלומין. Here סוכות is compared to פסח for לינה. The rule for סוכות is borrowed from פסח, so the next question naturally asks where פסח gets this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival of מצות, i.e., פסח
Staying overnight (in ירושלים after bringing the offerings)
Just as ... so too (the formula of a comparison)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one verse that groups the רגלים together can transfer specific laws from פסח to the other festivals.

phrases.english: Just as the festival of matzos requires staying overnight —
phrases.notes: This is the case we learn from: פסח.

phrases.english: so too the festival of Sukkos requires staying overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה חַג הַמַּצּוֹת טָעוּן לִינָה אַף חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת טָעוּן לִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a דרשה begun on the previous amud (the היקש of שבועות and סוכות to פסח)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוכות requires לינה in ירושלים, learned from its comparison to פסח.

steps.title: Where do we know פסח requires staying overnight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that פסח itself requires לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there (regarding פסח), from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a background question. Where do we learn that פסח requires לינה in the first place? This sets up the next step, which gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the original case's rule is firmly grounded. סוכות borrowed לינה from פסח, so the גמרא wants to see where פסח got it.

keyTerms.meaning: There (referring to the source case, פסח)
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: "There" means פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule that was used as the base of the comparison in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that פסח requires לינה

steps.title: The verse: turn in the morning and go to your tents
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק "ופנית בבקר והלכת לאהליך". You go home only in the morning, so you must stay the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about the קרבן פסח. It tells the person to go home only in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah says you leave "in the morning," then you must have spent the night in ירושלים. That is the לינה requirement for פסח, which was then extended to סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall turn (to leave) in the morning
To your tents, i.e., your homes

steps.whatToRemember: פסח requires לינה because of "ופנית בבקר." Through the היקש, סוכות requires it too.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And you shall turn in the morning
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ז, said about the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: and go to your tents."
phrases.notes: Leaving only in the morning implies staying overnight

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "ופנית בבקר והלכת לאהליך" shows that one leaves only in the morning, so staying the night is required.

steps.title: Where do the other תנאים learn make-up days for שבועות?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון use the verse for a different purpose. So where do they learn that שבועות has seven days of תשלומין?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון (בן אלעזר) — from where do they derive make-up days for עצרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinions in the ברייתא. They used the verse "בחג המצות ובחג השבועות ובחג הסוכות" to teach the order of the רגלים for בל תאחר. So they need a different source for שבועות having seven make-up days. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The derasha that compared שבועות to פסח for תשלומין belonged to the opinion that had this verse free for that purpose. The other תנאים used the verse up for בל תאחר. Everyone agrees שבועות has תשלומין for seven days, so the גמרא asks for their source.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) תנא of the ברייתא
Make-up days for bringing the festival offerings
From where do they derive it?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the people. The "רבי שמעון" here is one of the תנאים who used the verse for בל תאחר. He is not the one who made the comparison to פסח. The words "בן אלעזר" are printed in parentheses, which shows the editors questioned them.

phrases.english: And the first Tanna and Rabbi Shimon (ben Elazar) —
phrases.notes: The parenthetical words are a bracketed textual note in the printed edition

phrases.english: make-up days for Atzeres, from where do they derive them?
phrases.notes: They already used the פסוק about the order of the festivals for בל תאחר, so they can't use it for this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן תַּשְׁלוּמִין לַעֲצֶרֶת מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the opinion that made the היקש to the other opinions, which lack that source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for seven days of תשלומין for שבועות according to the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל: עצרת is sanctified for a full week, like the month for a day
steps.stepSummary: They learn it from רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא. Counting days and then sanctifying applies to both ראש חודש and עצרת. Each is sanctified for its counting unit: one day for the month, one week for עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They derive it from what רבה בר שמואל taught. For רבה בר שמואל taught: The תורה said, count days and sanctify the month; count days and sanctify עצרת. Just as the month is sanctified for its counting unit, so too עצרת is sanctified for its counting unit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these תנאים learn שבועות's seven make-up days from a ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל. It compares עצרת to ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We count days to reach ראש חודש, and the month is sanctified for one day, the unit we count in. For עצרת we count weeks ("שבע שבתות תמימות"), so עצרת is sanctified for a unit of one week. That gives seven days in which its offerings can still be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: According to its counting unit (day for the month, week for עצרת)

steps.whatToRemember: Even without the verse comparing it to פסח, שבועות has seven days of תשלומין. It is counted in weeks, so it is sanctified for a full week.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practical law that the חגיגה and ראיה offerings of שבועות may be brought during a seven-day period: the day of the holiday plus six make-up days. This holds even though the holiday itself is one day.

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מִדְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: They derive it from what Rabba bar Shmuel taught.
For Rabba bar Shmuel taught:
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה מְנֵה יָמִים וְקַדֵּשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: The Torah said: count days and sanctify the month;
phrases.notes: The פסוק says "חודש ימים" (במדבר יא:כ), so a month is counted in days.

phrases.english: count days and sanctify Atzeres.
phrases.notes: "תספרו חמשים יום" (ויקרא כג:טז)

phrases.english: Just as the month is sanctified according to its counting unit —
phrases.notes: One day

phrases.english: so too Atzeres according to its counting unit.
phrases.notes: Its unit is a week ("שבע שבתות"), so it gets seven days of תשלומין.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מִדְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with an independent source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עצרת is compared to ראש חודש. Each is sanctified for its counting unit, and עצרת's unit is a week, so it has seven days of תשלומין.

steps.title: Maybe the counting unit for שבועות is only one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 5: since we count days to עצרת, maybe it should be sanctified for one day only.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that עצרת has only one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that עצרת is sanctified for a week. If we count days until עצרת, maybe its unit is one day, like ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, each holiday was sanctified for the unit it is counted by. But we count fifty days until עצרת, so the counting unit seems to be days. That would mean only one day of תשלומין, not seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe I should say (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: Say that Atzeret is only one day?
phrases.notes: Since we count days, maybe the unit of sanctification is a single day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 5 that עצרת is sanctified for a week.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עצרת is counted in weeks and so gets seven days of תשלומין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We count days to עצרת, so by step 5's own rule its unit should be one day.

steps.title: רבא: we count weeks too, not only days
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that there is also a מצוה to count weeks. So the unit of עצרת can be a week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do we count only days for עצרת and not weeks? But the Master said: it is a מצוה to count days, and it is a מצוה to count weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. We do not count only days; there is also a מצוה to count weeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the count was only in days. רבא brings a statement that we also count weeks. Since weeks are counted too, עצרת is sanctified for a week, giving seven days of תשלומין.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (rejects an assumption)
But didn't the Master say (quotes a known teaching)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is that to say that for Atzeret we count days,
and we do not count weeks?
But didn't the Master say:
It is a מצוה to count days,
and it is a מצוה to count weeks.
phrases.notes: Because weeks are counted, the week is a valid unit for עצרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַטּוּ עֲצֶרֶת יוֹמֵי מָנִינַן, שָׁבוּעֵי לָא מָנִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenger's assumption by citing a known teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We count only days to עצרת, so its unit is one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: We count weeks as well, so עצרת is sanctified for a week.

steps.title: Extra proof: the Torah calls it the festival of weeks
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a second proof: the פסוק calls the holiday חג שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another proof from the Torah's own name for the holiday. It is called the festival of weeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name חג שבועות shows that the holiday is defined by weeks, not days. This supports giving it a full week of תשלומין.
steps.whatToRemember: עצרת has seven days of תשלומין because its counting unit is the week: we count weeks, and the Torah calls it חג שבועות.

phrases.english: And furthermore, "the festival of weeks" is written.
phrases.notes: The holiday is named for weeks, so a week is its unit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, Torah-based support to רבא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That עצרת is sanctified for a week.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק's name for the holiday: חג שבועות.

steps.title: How can the Paschal lamb be delayed past the festivals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא of בל תאחר, which lists פסח. It asks how פסח can be delayed if it has a fixed day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is פסח fit to be offered on the רגלים? פסח has a fixed time. If he offered it, he offered it. If he did not offer it, it is pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא that listed פסח among things that can break בל תאחר. It asks how that is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תאחר means delaying an offering past three רגלים. But קרבן פסח can only be brought on the fourteenth of ניסן. If that day passes, it can never be brought, so it cannot be delayed through later festivals.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. We are no longer talking about תשלומין of עצרת. The גמרא has returned to the ברייתא listing which offerings fall under בל תאחר.

phrases.english: But is the Paschal lamb fit to be offered on the festivals?
The Paschal lamb has a fixed time,
phrases.notes: The fourteenth of ניסן.

phrases.english: if he offered it, he offered it,
and if he did not offer it, it is pushed off!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עצרת discussion and returns to an item in the ברייתא of בל תאחר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of פסח among offerings that can break בל תאחר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח has one fixed day. Once that passes, it is pushed off forever, so it can never be delayed through three רגלים.

steps.title: רב חסדא: פסח was mentioned for no real reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that פסח was listed in the ברייתא without real meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: פסח was mentioned for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He says the ברייתא mentioned פסח, but it does not actually belong to the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא admits the question is right: בל תאחר does not apply to פסח. It was mentioned only because בכור, מעשר and פסח are often listed together.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The Paschal lamb was mentioned for no reason.
phrases.notes: It was listed out of habit, alongside בכור and מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: פֶּסַח כְּדִי נַסְבֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains away the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means that בל תאחר applies to the קרבן פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח was mentioned without real legal meaning. בל תאחר does not apply to it.

steps.title: רב ששת: it means the peace-offering of Pesach
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives another answer: the ברייתא's word פסח means שלמי פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What is "פסח"? The שלמי פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a different answer. He reads the word פסח in the ברייתא as the peace-offering that comes from a פסח animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פסח animal was lost and replaced, then later found, it is brought as a שלמים. That שלמים has no fixed day, so it can be delayed past three רגלים. So the ברייתא is fully accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: A peace-offering brought from an animal set aside as a פסח

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the ברייתא lists פסח: רב חסדא says it was mentioned for no reason, and רב ששת says it means שלמי פסח, which can be delayed.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What is "Pesach"? The peace-offering of the Paschal lamb.
phrases.notes: A peace-offering with no fixed day, so it can be delayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: מַאי ״פֶּסַח״ — שַׁלְמֵי פֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 9, different from רב חסדא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח in the ברייתא means the actual קרבן פסח, which has a fixed day.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח means שלמי פסח, which has no fixed day, so בל תאחר truly applies.

steps.title: If it means peace-offerings, it is already listed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: if פסח in the ברייתא means שלמי פסח, that is just שלמים, which the ברייתא already listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as peace-offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer. If the ברייתא's word פסח really means peace-offerings, it would be a needless repeat, because peace-offerings are already on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of בל תאחר already lists שלמים as one of the offerings you must not delay. If פסח only means שלמי פסח, the ברייתא seems to say the same thing twice. A ברייתא is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason, so רב ששת's reading looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from the last answer
The prohibition against delaying offerings you have pledged

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If פסח means שלמי פסח, as רב ששת said.

phrases.english: this is the same as peace-offerings!
phrases.notes: Peace-offerings were already listed in the ברייתא, so this would be a repeat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading that the ברייתא's word פסח means שלמי פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already lists שלמים. Reading פסח as שלמים makes the ברייתא repeat itself for no reason.

steps.title: Two kinds of peace-offerings, and why both were needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists two different kinds of שלמים: those that come because of פסח and those that come on their own. The גמרא begins explaining why both were needed: you might have thought that peace-offerings tied to פסח follow a different rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא taught peace-offerings that come because of פסח, and it taught peace-offerings that come on their own. It would have entered your mind to say: since they come because of פסח...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת by saying the ברייתא is not repeating itself. It lists two different types of peace-offerings, and it starts to explain the mistake we might have made without the second listing. That explanation finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general word שלמים covers ordinary peace-offerings a person brings on his own. שלמי פסח are peace-offerings connected to the פסח. Because they are tied to the פסח, we might have thought they share the פסח's own rules, so the ברייתא needed to mention them separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the פסח; connected to the Paschal offering
On their own; independent, not tied to anything else
It would have entered your mind to say: introduces a mistaken first assumption

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is finishing its point here. The sentence 'since they come because of פסח...' is only the start of the reasoning. Its conclusion comes on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic method of the גמרא: an apparent repeat in a ברייתא is resolved by showing that each item teaches something new.

phrases.english: It taught peace-offerings
phrases.notes: The first kind on the list.

phrases.english: that come because of the Paschal offering,
phrases.notes: This is what the word פסח in the ברייתא refers to.

phrases.english: and it taught peace-offerings
phrases.notes: The second kind on the list.

phrases.english: that come on their own.
phrases.notes: This is what the plain word שלמים in the ברייתא refers to.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:
phrases.notes: Introduces the mistaken assumption that made both listings necessary.

phrases.english: since they come because of the Paschal offering,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת פֶּסַח וּתְנָא שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of Step 12 and defends רב ששת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two categories within one term: the ברייתא's two mentions refer to different kinds of שלמים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Peace-offerings that come because of the פסח might follow the פסח's own rules (this is being set up and finishes on the next amud).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is not redundant. It teaches בל תאחר separately for independent שלמים and for שלמים tied to the פסח.
